intro.text: A man who comes to Clubs' shop as Kelsier and his crew plan to bring down the Final Empire, and with whom Kelsier talks alone while Vin eavesdrops.
Kelsier's brother, a Seeker who agreed to infiltrate the Steel Ministry to help Kelsier's plan against the Lord Ruler.
Kelsier's brother, a Seeker who infiltrated the Steel Ministry for the rebellion and was turned into a Steel Inquisitor.
Ironeyes, a mythical figure in Elendel's popular culture, seen as the personification of Death.
Kelsier's brother, still alive in 348 PC but weakening and aging as his supply of atium runs low.

items.text: Like Kelsier, Marsh hated injustice and led the skaa rebellion for years, while his brother ran a thieving crew. Marsh also loved Mare, who married Kelsier instead. After Kelsier and Mare were caught during a heist and sent to the Pits of Hathsin, where Mare died, Marsh gave up on the rebellion as dangerous and futile.

When Kelsier escaped the Pits as a Mistborn with a new plan to overthrow the Lord Ruler, Marsh doubted his motives and suspected it was still a game to him. Still loving his brother, and wanting to finally make a difference, he agreed to infiltrate the Steel Ministry, hoping his Seeker abilities would help him get in.
Marsh was the one who first noticed Vin's instinctive Allomancy and suggested, through Dockson, that she might be Mistborn, which led Kelsier to recruit her. He also taught her about bronze.

Slipping in among a group of new Ministry recruits arriving in Luthadel, Marsh was accepted and began passing secrets to the rebellion through hidden messages and drop sites, including the locations of soothing stations that kept the skaa docile and despairing.

Marsh arranged a meeting at a site he was meant to inspect, but the crew found only a headless corpse butchered by Inquisitors and believed him dead. A message hidden in a chair leg warned that his questions about the Inquisitors had drawn their attention.
In truth, the Inquisitors had wanted him because he was a Seeker and had turned him into an Inquisitor himself, strengthening his bronze abilities. Even so, he kept helping the rebellion in secret.

After the Lord Ruler's fall, Marsh, behaving strangely, led Sazed to the Conventical of Seran. There Sazed found Kwaan's metal inscription, but Marsh would not let him translate it on the spot, forcing him to take a rubbing instead, and then fled and vanished.
After the siege of Luthadel, Marsh, increasingly aware his actions were not his own, appeared again to stop Sazed from warning Vin about giving up the power at the Well of Ascension.

Once Ruin was freed, it took almost complete control of Marsh's body. Trapped in his own mind, he hoped to pull out a key spike and end his life when Ruin was distracted, but never managed more than a twitch. Ruin gave him many more spikes to tighten its hold, making him the most powerful of the Inquisitors.

During Vin's battle with the Inquisitors at Kredik Shaw, Marsh's buried will resurfaced. Aided by Kelsier, he tore out Vin's earring, letting the mists and Preservation's power flow into her so she could destroy the other Inquisitors. He survived only because she Ascended just before removing his second head spike.
Under Ruin's control once more, Marsh was sent to the Battle of Hathsin, where he beheaded the exhausted Elend.
A shadowy figure known as Ironeyes used emotional Allomancy to make Marasi curious enough to follow him, then gave her a book about Hemalurgy to deliver to Wax.

By 348 PC, Marsh's atium was running low and age was catching up with him. Desperate for more, he searched Bilming, where the Set was trying to recreate the metal, not because he wanted to live but to keep doing good as penance for his part in the world's destruction.

Two years after Autonomy's retreat, Marsh, his health improving thanks to new atium created when Harmonium was split, met Wax, Steris and Marasi in the Field of Rebirth to hand Wax a letter from Harmony, since Wax had forbidden mental contact.
Marsh met with Khriss and explained Hemalurgy, Compounding and Inquisitors to her. Stories of him spread to other worlds; on Lumar, Death was imagined with nails in his eyes.

appearance.text: In 348 PC he looked thin and skeletal, with ghostly skin, seeming to age and grow younger by decades with each breath. He wore black robes or a black trench coat and brimmed hat, and spoke with a very old accent.

personality.text: Marsh hated injustice. He was uneasy with Kelsier's eagerness to kill nobles and their servants and his flippant attitude about it, seeing his brother as frivolous and self-important, yet he stayed loyal to him. His love for Mare never faded.

After being spiked he grew detached from his emotions and acted strangely. Under Ruin's control he was malicious and sadistic, but in rare lucid moments he repeatedly tried to kill himself so Ruin could no longer use him.

Marsh has no wish to live for his own sake but keeps going as penance, wanting to do good to make up for deaths Ruin forced on him. He likes hearing his name, which reminds him of who he was, and sees the three surviving members of the original crew as a tripod that must stay balanced.
He feels a kinship with others who have been spiked, calling Wax his brother, and serves Harmony with deep respect.
